s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques on the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms have been present for more than 10 years
Lesions are localized to the left shin
Lesions are itchy
Milia are present in the superficial dermis
Erosions with partially detached epidermis are present
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination reveals dermoepidermal separation
Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1

differentials: Epidermolysis Bullosa with Congenital Localized Absence of Skin
Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa with Specific Ultrastructural Defects
per_call: Epidermolysis Bullosa with Congenital Localized Absence of Skin
Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa with Specific Ultrastructural Defects

shortlist.label: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1, which is a common cause of this condition

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Pruriginosa
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with itchy skin lesions and milia, which are characteristic features of this condition

shortlist.label: Kindler Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has dermoepidermal separation and milia, which are also seen in Kindler Syndrome

shortlist.label: Recessive Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa, but with a recessive inheritance pattern

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, this condition can also present with itchy skin lesions and milia

raw.rationale: The presence of pruritic, lichenified papules and plaques, along with the localization to a specific area and the long duration of symptoms, are characteristic of Epidermolysis Bullosa Pruriginosa, a subtype of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.

rejected.label: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: Too broad, as the specific characteristics of the case point towards a more specific subtype.

rejected.label: Kindler Syndrome
rejected.why: Involves more extensive extracutaneous manifestations and earlier onset, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Recessive Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: The genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant, suggesting an autosomal dominant pattern, not recessive.

rejected.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
rejected.why: Typically presents with more generalized skin fragility and blisters, not localized itchy papules and plaques as seen in this case.
